question: True or false: people can see flicker artefacts on a display refreshing 500 times a second?
answer: True. In a 2015 study, viewers spotted artefacts at 500 Hz when their eyes swept across a high-contrast edge: each flash landed on a different spot of the retina, leaving a trail of copies. With a steady gaze, flicker fuses near 50 to 90 Hz. A sweeping eye turns flashes into a dotted line.
move: A threshold found in one condition is not a threshold in all of them.
trap: False, anchored on the idea that eyes top out near 60 Hz.
